newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN BACOB BANK IN PARTNER SEARCH - CEO.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN BACOB BANK IN PARTNER SEARCH - CEO.

text.p: Bacob Bank, Belgium's seventh-largest bank, is looking for a foreign partner in preparation for the advent of the single currency, its chief executive officer Dirk Bruneel said on Thursday.

"We are looking for a partner, in France, Germany, the Netherlands and Austria. A partner which looks like us -- that is, with a strong local representation, a good client base, and who can help us develop niche activities," Bruneel told journalists at a press briefing.
"We are already in talks with a number of potential partners, though we are not close to finalising a deal."

"Soon the euro market will be there, which in the minimal scenario will be bigger than the yen market, and in the maximum scenario bigger than the dollar market. Competition will increase, mega banks will see the light. We cannot sit on our hands," Bruneel said.
"We are looking for a player with a good local base, but who is not so strong on the international markets. We are looking for a partner to form a network," he added.
He said his bank has been on the lookout for one and a half years.
Bruneel said it was more likely Bacob would take a stake in a foreign bank than that a foreign bank would take a stake in Bacob.
He added that last year, Bacob's cooperative shareholders had provided it with three billion francs worth of new capital.
"We are stocking up on ammunition," he said.
Bacob, which is linked to the Belgian Christian Workers' Movement, has a cooperative shareholding structure which would be difficult to enter for a foreign partner.
Bacob is 65.6 percent held by Arcofin, a holding company controlled by the christian-democratic Arco group.
Bacob customers hold 29.9 percent of Bacob, while personnel holds 4.5 percent.
"There is a future for smaller banks, provided that they pool their know-how," Bruneel said.
Bacob has already made a few fruitless attempts at teaming up with other players.

In the summer of 1995 it made an unsuccesful bid for Belgian industrial credit bank NMKN/SNCI. Earlier this year, Bacob was part of an international consortium which made an unsuccesfull bid for Austrian Creditanstalt.
Bruneel discarded the possibility of a stock market introduction for Bacob.
"That is a capitalistic concept of property which does not fit our group," he said.

"It would not be proper for Bacob to be Belgium's most profitable bank, because that would mean we did not give enough to our cooperative members. What our partner search is concerned, we will feel better if our partner has a management which is not only shareholder-driven," Bruneel said.
Bruneel also said that Bacob would publish 1996 earnings growth of about 30 percent on March 28.
In 1995, Bacob earned a 2.24 billion franc net profit.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
